_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Israel covering Canaanite period, Israelite kingdoms (David, Solomon), Babylonian exile, Second Temple period, Roman province (Judea), Jewish revolts, Byzantine Palestine, Arab conquest, Crusader states, Mamluk/Ottoman Palestine, Zionism, British Mandate, 1948 Declaration of Independence, Arab-Israeli wars, Six-Day War 1967, Yom Kippur War 1973, Camp David Accords, Oslo Accords, intifadas, settlements, and ongoing Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

ethnic_groups.name: Jewish Israeli
ethnic_groups.notes: Diverse origins: Ashkenazi (European/US ~44% of Jews), Mizrahi/Sephardi (Middle East/North Africa ~44%), Ethiopian (Beta Israel ~2%), mixed; Hebrew-speaking; Law of Return

ethnic_groups.name: Arab Israeli (Palestinian citizens)
ethnic_groups.notes: Arabic-speaking; mostly Muslim, also Christian and Druze; remained after 1948; citizens with voting rights; identity tension; Bedouin sub-group in Negev (~280,000)

ethnic_groups.name: Druze
ethnic_groups.notes: Galilee and Golan Heights; distinct monotheistic faith; serve in IDF; loyal to state; ~148,000

ethnic_groups.name: Circassian
ethnic_groups.notes: Two villages (Kfar Kama, Rehaniya); Sunni Muslim; serve in IDF; arrived Ottoman era

ethnic_groups.name: Other (foreign workers, asylum seekers)
ethnic_groups.notes: Thai, Filipino, Chinese workers; Eritrean/Sudanese asylum seekers (~25,000); Russian non-Jewish immigrants

independence.notes: Declaration by David Ben-Gurion; immediately followed by 1948 Arab-Israeli War

country_profile.notes_unique: Only Jewish-majority state; nuclear-armed (undeclared); 'Start-Up Nation'; Iron Dome missile defence; Dead Sea lowest point on Earth; kibbutz movement; ongoing occupation of West Bank (since 1967)
special_status_languages: Arabic (formerly official, now 'special status' since 2018 Nation-State Law)

current_leader.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
current_leader.title: Prime Minister
current_leader.notes: Likud; longest-serving PM; corruption trial; far-right coalition; judicial overhaul crisis 2023; October 7 Hamas attack 2023; Gaza War 2023-2025; ICC arrest warrant

president.name: Isaac Herzog
president.title: President (ceremonial)
president.notes: Son of Chaim Herzog (6th president); Labour background

former_leaders.name: David Ben-Gurion
former_leaders.notes: Founder; Mapai; declared independence; first PM; built state institutions; immigration absorption

former_leaders.name: Golda Meir
former_leaders.notes: Labour; 'Iron Lady' before Thatcher; Yom Kippur War 1973 nearly lost; resigned

former_leaders.name: Menachem Begin
former_leaders.notes: Likud; first right-wing PM; Camp David Accords/peace with Egypt 1979; Nobel Prize; invaded Lebanon 1982

former_leaders.name: Yitzhak Rabin
former_leaders.notes: Labour; Oslo Accords with PLO; Nobel Prize 1994; assassinated by Jewish extremist November 4, 1995

former_leaders.name: Ariel Sharon
former_leaders.notes: Likud then Kadima; controversial general; Gaza disengagement 2005; incapacitating stroke January 2006; died 2014

former_leaders.name: Ehud Barak
former_leaders.notes: Labour; most decorated soldier; Camp David 2000 (failed); withdrew from Lebanon 2000

910.name: Canaanite and Bronze Age Levant
910.description: The Canaanite city-states of the Bronze Age, their role in the Egyptian sphere of influence, the Amarna Letters, and the upheavals of the Bronze Age collapse.

sub_clusters.name: Canaanite City-States
sub_clusters.description: The urban Canaanite civilization with major centers at Megiddo, Hazor, Jericho, and Lachish, their trade networks, and the development of the proto-Sinaitic alphabet.
key_events: Megiddo and Hazor emerge as major Canaanite city-states
Development of the proto-Sinaitic/Canaanite alphabet — ancestor of all alphabets (c. 1800 BC)

sub_clusters.name: Egyptian Domination and Amarna Period
sub_clusters.description: Canaan under Egyptian New Kingdom control, the Amarna Letters revealing the political dynamics of Canaanite vassal kings, and the arrival of the Sea Peoples disrupting the region.

910.name: Ancient Israelite Kingdoms
910.description: The emergence of ancient Israel, the united monarchy of David and Solomon, the divided kingdoms of Israel and Judah, and the Babylonian exile.

sub_clusters.name: Israelite Emergence and United Monarchy
sub_clusters.description: The emergence of Israelite identity in the central highlands, the biblical narrative of the united monarchy under Saul, David, and Solomon, and the construction of the First Temple in Jerusalem.
key_events: King David establishes Jerusalem as capital (c. 1000 BC)
Solomon builds the First Temple in Jerusalem (c. 960 BC)

sub_clusters.name: Divided Kingdoms and Babylonian Exile
sub_clusters.description: The split into the northern Kingdom of Israel and southern Kingdom of Judah, the Assyrian destruction of Israel, and Nebuchadnezzar's conquest of Judah and destruction of the First Temple.
key_events: Assyria conquers the Kingdom of Israel and deports the Ten Tribes (722 BC)
Nebuchadnezzar II destroys Jerusalem and the First Temple; Babylonian Exile begins (586 BC)

910.name: Second Temple Period
910.description: The return from exile, the rebuilding of the Temple, Hellenistic influence, the Maccabean revolt, the Hasmonean kingdom, Roman rule, and the destruction of the Second Temple.

sub_clusters.name: Persian Return and Hellenistic Period
sub_clusters.description: Cyrus' decree allowing Jewish return, the rebuilding of the Second Temple, Persian Yehud province, and the Hellenistic period under Ptolemaic and Seleucid rule.

sub_clusters.name: Maccabees and Hasmonean Kingdom
sub_clusters.description: The Maccabean revolt against Seleucid religious persecution, the rededication of the Temple (Hanukkah), and the independent Hasmonean kingdom.
key_events: Maccabean revolt and rededication of the Temple — origin of Hanukkah (164 BC)

sub_clusters.name: Roman Judea and Second Temple Destruction
sub_clusters.description: Pompey's conquest, Herod the Great's massive building projects including the expansion of the Second Temple, the ministry of Jesus of Nazareth, and the Roman destruction of the Temple.
key_events: Herod the Great massively expands the Second Temple complex (c. 20 BC)
Roman legions under Titus destroy the Second Temple in Jerusalem (70 AD)

920.name: Roman-Byzantine Palestine
920.description: The Bar Kokhba revolt, the Romanization of Judea as 'Palaestina,' the rise of Christianity under Constantine, Byzantine church building, and the transition to Arab rule.

sub_clusters.name: Bar Kokhba Revolt and Diaspora
sub_clusters.description: The Great Revolt's aftermath, the Bar Kokhba rebellion of 132–136 AD, Hadrian's renaming of the province to Syria Palaestina, the ban on Jews in Jerusalem, and the growth of the diaspora.
key_events: Bar Kokhba revolt — last major Jewish uprising against Rome (132–136 AD)
Hadrian renames the province Syria Palaestina and rebuilds Jerusalem as Aelia Capitolina

sub_clusters.name: Byzantine Christian Holy Land
sub_clusters.description: Constantine's Christianization, Helena's identification of holy sites, the construction of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, the Samaritan revolts, and the brief Sassanid occupation.

920.name: Early Islamic and Crusader Periods
920.description: The Arab conquest and the building of the Dome of the Rock, the Crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem, Saladin's reconquest, and the final Mamluk expulsion of the Crusaders.

sub_clusters.name: Arab Conquest and Dome of the Rock
sub_clusters.description: Umar's conquest of Jerusalem, the construction of the Dome of the Rock and Al-Aqsa Mosque on the Temple Mount, the Fatimid period, and the lead-up to the Crusades.
key_events: Caliph Umar captures Jerusalem (637 AD)
Dome of the Rock completed on the Temple Mount (691 AD)

sub_clusters.name: Crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem
sub_clusters.description: The First Crusade's capture of Jerusalem, the Latin Kingdom and its feudal structure, Saladin's victory at Hattin, and the final fall of Acre ending two centuries of Crusader presence.
key_events: First Crusade captures Jerusalem; massacre of Muslim and Jewish inhabitants (1099)
Saladin defeats the Crusaders at the Battle of Hattin and recaptures Jerusalem (1187)

930.name: Mamluk Palestine
930.description: Palestine under Mamluk Egyptian rule, the defeat of the Mongols at Ain Jalut, the marginalization of the region as a provincial backwater, and the small Jewish communities in Safed and Jerusalem.

sub_clusters.name: Mamluk Rule and Mongol Defeat
sub_clusters.description: The Mamluk victory over the Mongols at Ain Jalut (1260) in the Jezreel Valley — one of history's most significant battles — and the consolidation of Mamluk control over Palestine.
key_events: Battle of Ain Jalut — Mamluks defeat the Mongols, saving the Islamic world (1260)

sub_clusters.name: Late Mamluk Decline
sub_clusters.description: The economic decline of Palestine under late Mamluk rule, Bedouin raids, plague outbreaks, and the small but persistent Jewish scholarly communities in Safed.

930.name: Ottoman Palestine
930.description: Palestine under Ottoman rule — Suleiman's rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls, the autonomous rule of Zahir al-Umar in Galilee, and Napoleon's abortive invasion.

sub_clusters.name: Early Ottoman and Suleiman Era
sub_clusters.description: Selim I's conquest from the Mamluks, Suleiman the Magnificent's reconstruction of Jerusalem's walls (the current Old City walls), and the development of the millet system.
key_events: Suleiman the Magnificent rebuilds Jerusalem's walls — the walls standing today (1535–1541)

sub_clusters.name: Zahir al-Umar and Napoleon's Invasion
sub_clusters.description: The autonomous rule of Zahir al-Umar in Galilee and Acre, Napoleon Bonaparte's failed siege of Acre in 1799, and the region's marginal status within the Ottoman Empire.

940.name: Late Ottoman Palestine and Early Zionism
940.description: The transformation of Palestine in the 19th century, the Tanzimat reforms, European interests, the birth of political Zionism, and the first Jewish immigration waves (aliyot).

sub_clusters.name: Nineteenth-Century Palestine
sub_clusters.description: Ottoman reforms, Egyptian occupation under Ibrahim Pasha (1831–1840), the opening of European consulates in Jerusalem, and the growth of the Jewish Yishuv community.

sub_clusters.name: Birth of Zionism and First Aliyot
sub_clusters.description: Theodor Herzl's publication of 'Der Judenstaat,' the First Zionist Congress, the First and Second Aliyah immigration waves, and the founding of Tel Aviv and Hebrew as a spoken language.
key_events: Theodor Herzl convenes the First Zionist Congress in Basel (1897)
Tel Aviv founded as the first modern Hebrew-speaking city (1909)

950.name: British Mandate Palestine
950.description: The Balfour Declaration, the British Mandate, Arab-Jewish intercommunal violence, WWII and the Holocaust, and the end of the Mandate.

sub_clusters.name: Balfour Declaration and Mandate
sub_clusters.description: The Balfour Declaration promising a Jewish national home, the League of Nations Mandate, growing Jewish immigration, and increasing Arab-Jewish tensions.
key_events: Balfour Declaration — Britain supports a Jewish national home in Palestine (1917)
Arab Revolt against British rule and Jewish immigration (1936–1939)

sub_clusters.name: WWII, Holocaust, and End of Mandate
sub_clusters.description: British White Paper restricting Jewish immigration, the Holocaust's destruction of European Jewry, illegal immigration (Aliyah Bet), the King David Hotel bombing, and the UN Partition Plan.
key_events: UN General Assembly votes for partition of Palestine into Jewish and Arab states (November 1947)

950.name: Establishment of Israel and Early State
950.description: The declaration of the State of Israel, the 1948 war, mass immigration, the Sinai Campaign, the Six-Day War, and the Yom Kippur War.

sub_clusters.name: 1948 War and Founding
sub_clusters.description: David Ben-Gurion's declaration of independence, the invasion by five Arab armies, the Israeli War of Independence / Palestinian Nakba, and the armistice agreements.
key_events: David Ben-Gurion declares the establishment of the State of Israel (May 14, 1948)
1948 Arab-Israeli War and the Palestinian Nakba — displacement of 700,000 Palestinians

sub_clusters.name: Six-Day War and Occupation
sub_clusters.description: The June 1967 war in which Israel captured the Sinai, Gaza, West Bank, East Jerusalem, and the Golan Heights — reshaping the conflict and beginning the occupation.
key_events: Six-Day War — Israel captures the West Bank, Gaza, Sinai, Golan Heights (June 1967)

sub_clusters.name: Yom Kippur War
sub_clusters.description: The surprise Egyptian-Syrian attack on Yom Kippur, initial Israeli setbacks, the eventual military recovery, and the war's catalytic effect on Israeli-Egyptian peace negotiations.

960.name: Peace Process and Contemporary Israel
960.description: The Camp David peace with Egypt, the Oslo Accords, the Second Intifada, settlement expansion, the Gaza wars, and the ongoing Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

sub_clusters.name: Camp David Accords and Lebanon Wars
sub_clusters.description: The historic peace treaty with Egypt, the 1982 Lebanon War and Sabra-Shatila massacre, the First Intifada, the Oslo Accords with the PLO, and Rabin's assassination.
key_events: Camp David Accords — first Arab-Israeli peace treaty with Egypt (1978)
Oslo Accords — mutual recognition between Israel and the PLO (1993)
Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin assassinated by an Israeli extremist (1995)

sub_clusters.name: Second Intifada and Disengagement
sub_clusters.description: The collapse of Camp David II talks, the Second Intifada, construction of the separation barrier, Sharon's unilateral withdrawal from Gaza, and the Hamas takeover of Gaza.

sub_clusters.name: Gaza Wars and Normalization
sub_clusters.description: Repeated military operations in Gaza, settlement expansion in the West Bank, the Abraham Accords normalization with Gulf states, and the October 7 2023 Hamas attack and subsequent war.
key_events: Abraham Accords — Israel normalizes relations with UAE, Bahrain, Morocco, Sudan (2020)
Hamas October 7 attack and subsequent Israeli military campaign in Gaza (2023)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
